question.text: The Ottomans conquered this capital city of the Byzantine Empire in May 1453. Give its name as of 1453, not its ancient name or its modern name, which was adopted in 1923.
question.answerHtml: Constantinople (do not accept or prompt on “Byzantium” or “Istanbul”)
question.clue: A road called the mese (MEH-say) ran through this city, which may have lost forty percent of its population in a plague in 542 CE. A gigantic cannon designed by Orban sufficed to break through this city's 60-foot-tall Theodosian Walls.

swap.text: The Byzantine Empire had several rulers with this common name; the first of whom usurped the throne from Michael III and founded the Macedonian dynasty, and the second was known as the Bulgar-slayer for his complete conquest of Bulgaria.
swap.clue: The Varangian Guard was expanded after a ruler of this name married his sister Anna to Vladimir I ("the first") of Kiev.

question.text: This Byzantine Emperor tasked Belisarius with reconquering the Mediterranean, and this husband of Theodora was targeted in the Nika Riots.
question.clue: This ruler was alleged to be a demon by the "Secret History" of his follower Procopius.

swap.text: Constantinople was earlier sacked during this campaign, which led to the decline of the Byzantine Empire. Enrico Dandolo, the Doge of Venice, had earlier led this campaign.
swap.clue: Pope Innocent III excommunicated all of its participants when they attacked the Dalmatian capital in exchange for assistance from Enrico Dandolo, the doge of Venice.

question.leadin: Name some things about the times when the use of religious images were opposed by both religious and Byzantine authority.
question.text: Name that time period during which depictions of religious figures was directly opposed by the leaders of the Eastern Church.
question.clue: This practice was carried out by mobs during the Dissolution of the Monasteries and again by the Puritans.

swap.leadin: This leader commissioned Isidore of Miletus to build the Hagia Sophia.
swap.text: Name this Byzantine Emperor of the 6th century C.E known as "the Great".
swap.clue: The scholar Tribonian headed a commission that published namesake "novels" that solved contradictions within a law code named for this ruler.

question.leadin: Before invading England, Harald Hardrada of Norway served as a mercenary in this military order.
question.text: Name this elite army unit that served as the personal bodyguards to the emperors of the Byzantine Empire.
question.clue: As punishment for replacing this group with loyal Scythians, Michael V ("the fifth") was castrated and blinded by Harald Hardrada.

swap.text: Justinian almost fled Constantinople during these riots that started after an angry crowd gathered at the Hippodrome.
swap.clue: Participants in this event wanted to crown Hypatius, but were outmaneuvered by the eunuch Narses and slaughtered by Mundus.

question.text: Michael VIII founded this dynasty, which expelled the Crusaders from Constantinople in 1261 and were the last to rule Byzantium before the Turkish conquest in 1453.
question.clue: The most famous member of this family temporarily ended the Great Schism with the Second Council of Lyon after reclaiming Constantinople from the Latin Empire. That man, Michael VIII, established this family as the final Byzantine dynasty.

swap.text: It saw the introduction of a new term for the nature of Christ, "en duo physesin." Called to refute the heresy of Eutyches, it met in 451. For 15 points, name this ecumenical council that condemned the Monophysite heresy.
swap.clue: Pope Leo I rejected Canon Twenty-Eight since it ran contradictory to previous canons from Nicaea.

question.text: One exception to the rule about unblemished features was the second Byzantine ruler of this name, who took the throne after exile despite having his nose cut off. Another Byzantine ruler of this name put down the Nika Revolt.
question.clue: Before his first overthrow, he lost the Battle of Sebastopolis to the Umayyads, after which this ruler ordered the butchering of all the Slavs in Bithynia.

swap.text: The "Eternal Peace" was signed after this Byzantine general defeated the Persians at the Battle of Dara. This general also conquered the Vandal kingdom and temporarily controlled Rome during the Gothic War.
swap.clue: Early in this leader's career, together with Mundus they were instrumental in ensuring Hypatius and Pompeius did not take the throne.

question.text: The Nika Riots occurred after opposition to the Justinian Code and other reforms led a mob to gather at one of these events before destroying much of Constantinople.
question.clue: Objects used in this activity include the biga ("BEE-gah") and quadriga ("KWAH-dree-gah").

swap.text: Disputes with the Byzantines over monastic funding partly convinced Tamar to install a ruler of this name as the first emperor of Trebizond. An earlier Komnenian king of this name called for assistance from the Crusaders against the Seljuk Turks.
swap.answerHtml: Alexios [or Alexius; accept Alexios I Megas Komnenos of Trebizond; accept Alexios I Komnenos]
swap.clue: One Byzantine ruler of this name sent emissaries to the Council of Piacenza in order to seek military aid. An account of that ruler with this name's reign was published by Anna Komnene, the daughter of that ruler.

question.leadin: Name some people whose writings serve as important primary sources about the Byzantine Empire.
question.text: This woman may have been inspired by the material laid out by her husband Nikephoros Bryennios the Younger to write a chronicle of her father's rule named the Alexiad.
question.clue: This twelfth-century Byzantine princess became one of the first known women historians by penning the Alexiad, which narrates the dynasty-establishing reign of her father Alexios I.

swap.text: After the Battle of Adrianople, the Bulgar tsar Kaloyan made a cup from the skull of the first Latin Emperor, who had this name. The final ruler of the Latin Empire, who sold the Crown of Thorns to Louis IX, also had this name.
swap.answerHtml: Baldwin [or Baudouin; or Baldwin I; or Baldwin II; or Baldwin of Courtenay]
swap.clue: This cousin of Rudyard Kipling highlighted the power of aerial attacks by noting that "the bomber will always get through."

question.leadin: This ruler recognized Stefan Nemanja ("NEH-mahn-yah") as the rightful zupan ("zhoo-pan") during an incredibly successful campaign through Serbia.
question.text: Identify this expansionist Byzantine emperor whose reign was chronicled by his loyal historian John Cinnamus. He magnanimously forgave Raynald of Chatillon ("shah-tee-YON") for his Cyprian massacre in exchange for total fealty.
question.clue: While this ruler's armies besieged the island of Corfu, the Venetians mocked this ruler by having an African slave impersonate him.

swap.text: The Sicilian Vespers were orchestrated in part by this Byzantine Emperor, who retook Constantinople from the Latin Empire and founded a namesake dynasty that ruled until 1453.
swap.answerHtml: Michael VIII Palaiologos [accept either of the second two underlined portions along with the first one; prompt on “Michael”]
swap.clue: This figure's diplomatic acumen and willingness to bankrupt his treasury helped Pedro III of Aragon, overthrowing Charles of Anjou in the Sicilian Vespers.

question.text: Psellos's Chronographia begins with the nearly-50-year reign of this emperor, who put down the rebellion of Bardas Skleros and forged a productive alliance with Vladimir I of the Kievan Rus.
question.answerHtml: Basil the Bulgar-Slayer [or Basil II; or Basileios II; or Basileios Boulgaroktonos; or Basil the Porphyrogenitus; or Basil the Young; prompt on “Basil”]
question.clue: After winning the Battle of Kleidion, this man ordered the blinding of 99 of every 100 prisoners of the defeated ethnicity, possibly inspiring his nickname.

swap.leadin: The last two church councils that dealt with this clause were the 1583 and 1672 Councils of Jerusalem.
swap.text: Identify this clause that was added to the Nicene Creed in 589 at the Council of Toledo. Its Latin name means "and the son," and it implies that the Holy Spirit proceeds from both God the father and his Son, Jesus. .
swap.clue: One of the major ideological differences between the two halves of the Church was the addition of this clause to the Nicene Creed. It states that the spirit proceeds from the "father and son" rather than just the "father".
